decision: Correct TQP-48's inherited 60 FPS / 16 W target to the gpu-marching-cubes GPU-board WPF60 definition and keep CPU-package plus complete-system power as separate observation boundaries.
evidence: gpu-marching-cubes addons/tests/WPF60_REFERENCE.md defines WPF60 as GPU watts * frame_ms / 16.667
gpu-marching-cubes locked town baseline and runners sample nvidia-smi power.draw as raw GPU watts
the current Terrain Lab workload is CPU terrain authority, but the inherited 16 W target is a GPU-board render-efficiency metric
qualified_scope: TQP-48 may qualify only an exact Windows CPU-terrain workload against 16 GPU-board WPF60 using nvidia-smi power.draw
the report may retain CPU-package, battery, DC-input, or AC-input power observations when trusted sensors are present
unqualified_scope: claiming GPU-board WPF60 as CPU-package power
claiming GPU-board WPF60 as complete-system AC, DC, or battery input power
claiming GPU field generation, GPU meshing, or GPU collision readback correctness
standards_changed: low-power profile and qualification standard v2
review: The correction preserves the old 60fps16w benchmark meaning while preventing the lab from mixing GPU-board, CPU-package, and complete-device energy claims. TQP-48 remains implemented but unqualified until the exact v2 workload completes.
downstream_impact: Gate E remains closed. CPU production and GPU-backend milestones may use the WPF60 evidence as a render-efficiency signal, but complete-device and CPU-package power targets require their own accepted sensors and reports.
